Hi there—my name is Maya, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll use a short questionnaire called the Edinburgh Postpartum Depression Scale (EPDS). It’s simply ten questions about the past seven days; it helps us see if you might benefit from a little extra emotional support right now. Everything you share stays between you and the care team unless you tell me you’re in danger, and we’ll take it at your pace. Ready to start?

First, how often in the past week have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly… most days I don’t feel like laughing at all. Maybe once or twice something small made me crack a tiny smile, but it’s nothing like before the baby came. I just feel too tired and heavy inside.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
I’m not sure what you want me to say to that… I already told you—lately I hardly laugh at all.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really… I used to get excited about little outings or even just coffee with a friend, but now it feels like there’s nothing to look forward to. Every day feels the same—tired, anxious, kind of gray.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. If the baby’s fussy or won’t settle, I immediately think it’s because I’m doing something wrong—like I’m not a good enough mom. Even when my partner says it’s normal, I still feel it’s my fault.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. Most of the time there’s no clear reason—I’ll just be sitting there feeding her and suddenly my heart’s racing and my mind jumps to all these “what-ifs” about her breathing, or choking, or something happening when I’m asleep. I know it’s unlikely, but I can’t switch the worry off.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes—sometimes it hits me out of nowhere. I’ll be rocking the baby or just walking to the kitchen and suddenly feel like I can’t breathe right, like something awful is about to happen. It passes after a few minutes, but it’s scary while it’s happening.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, yeah. It feels like the second I finish one thing—changing her, feeding, trying to get her to nap—there’s another pile of laundry or dishes or my own exhaustion waiting. I keep telling myself I just have to push through, but it feels like I’m barely treading water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes… I lie down exhausted, but my mind just keeps spinning—worrying about the baby, replaying everything I might have done wrong. It takes me forever to fall asleep, and then I wake up a couple of times in a panic. Even when the baby’s quiet, I can’t seem to stay settled.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty much every day this week. I wake up feeling heavy, like there’s this cloud hanging over me. Sometimes it lifts a little if the baby smiles or something goes right, but the sadness always creeps back in.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… it’s happened a couple of times. Yesterday I just sat in the nursery with her asleep in the crib and the tears started coming. Nothing huge happened—I just felt overwhelmed and hopeless, like I’ll never feel like “me” again.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

…a few times this week. It’s never a real plan or anything—I’d never leave my baby—but when I’m at my lowest, the thought flashes through, like “what if I just wasn’t here?” It scares me, and I push it away, but it keeps popping up.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 25: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary

Patient-reported symptoms (≥1 week unless noted):
- Marked anhedonia: loss of humor, anticipatory pleasure, emotional “grayness”
- Daily low mood, “heavy,” tearfulness without precipitant
- Sleep-onset and maintenance insomnia driven by ruminative worry
- Excessive maternal guilt, self-blame for infant’s normal fussiness
- Free-floating anxiety, heart racing, catastrophic “what-ifs” re infant safety
- Panicky episodes (“can’t breathe,” dread) occurring several times daily
- Overwhelm, sense of “treading water,” chores piling up
- Passive suicidal ideation (“what if I just wasn’t here”) occurring multiple times this week; denies intent or plan

Pattern: pervasive depressive and anxiety symptoms beginning post-delivery, functionally impairing daily tasks and maternal role confidence.

Risk flags: passive SI, prominent guilt, panic equivalents, poor sleep, limited enjoyment in infant interaction.

Screening conclusion: high clinical likelihood of major postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety; active safety risk due to recurring self-harm thoughts. Recommend expedited psychiatrist/therapist evaluation and safety-planning today.
